# Agentic Coding in the Wild: Characterizing GitHub Copilot at Production Scale

> A visual reading of the first production-scale characterization of an AI coding agent: sampled GitHub Copilot traces covering 13.5M sessions, 3.2M users and 760.5M LLM calls.

A reading, by Kiran Hombal (https://kstark007.github.io/), of the paper of the same
name by Banruo Liu, Haoran Qiu, Íñigo Goiri, Rodrigo Fonseca, Ricardo Bianchini, Esha Choukse. Every number on the page is transcribed from that
paper and cites the table or figure it came from; the 23 charts are
redrawn from curve geometry recovered from the paper's own vector figures,
not eyeballed.

## Read this instead of the HTML

- [Full post as markdown](https://kstark007.github.io/blog/agentic-coding-in-the-wild/index.md): the complete prose plus every figure and table as data.
- [Figure data](https://kstark007.github.io/blog/agentic-coding-in-the-wild/figure-data.json): recovered curve geometry for all 23 plots, as JSON.
- [The paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00101): arXiv:2608.00101, the primary source for everything here.

## Canonical locations

## What the paper measured

- Sessions: 13.5M
- User turns: 95.1M
- Users: 3.2M
- LLM calls: 760.5M
- Tool calls: 774.7M
- Prompt tokens: 44.9T
- Completion tokens: 39.3B
- Models / tools: 27+ / 45+

Source: anonymized GitHub Copilot coding-agent telemetry.
Surfaces: Visual Studio and VS Code. Window: First week of June 2026.
Structural metadata only — timings, token counts, model and tool names,
success and failure. No prompts, no code, no user identity.
